product_description: A comprehensive, open-source guide for preparing for JavaScript interviews. Includes hundreds of questions, answers, and coding challenges covering core JS concepts, React, Node.js, and general web development.
crisis_comment:
Technical interviews can be incredibly stressful, and it's completely normal to feel overwhelmed.

If it helps, I've put together a comprehensive, free open-source guide for JavaScript interviews. It breaks down hundreds of concepts and questions to help you prepare methodically:
https://g-h-0-s-t.github.io/JavaScript-Interview/

Take it one topic at a time. You've got this.
voice_rules: Be encouraging and academic, positioning yourself as a fellow developer sharing resources
Always mention the guide is free and open-source
Focus on how the guide structures learning (e.g., 'breaks down core concepts')
Use signature closings: 'Happy coding', 'Good luck with the prep', 'You'll do great'
Keep it conversational but technical enough to show authority
anti_patterns: No 'guaranteed to pass' or 'crack the interview' promises
Never imply they should know something already

voice_seeds.text:
If you're gearing up for frontend roles, the sheer volume of JavaScript concepts to review can be daunting.

I built a comprehensive, free open-source guide that covers everything from core JS to React and Node.js. It's structured to help you study methodically rather than just memorizing answers.

Check it out here: https://g-h-0-s-t.github.io/JavaScript-Interview/

Happy coding.

The hardest part of JS interviews is that they can ask you anything from the event loop to React rendering lifecycles.

I compiled a free guide that breaks down hundreds of these exact questions and concepts, complete with code examples.

It's completely open-source: https://g-h-0-s-t.github.io/JavaScript-Interview/

Good luck with the prep.

Prepping for a technical round?

Here is a massive, free open-source repository of JavaScript interview questions and explanations I put together:
https://g-h-0-s-t.github.io/JavaScript-Interview/

Hope it helps. You'll do great.
